sections.skill: Compare employee and independent contractor work and estimate gig income after expenses and taxes

questions.prompt: Ravi drives for a delivery app as an independent contractor. Which statement is TRUE for him but NOT for a typical employee?

choices.text: No taxes are withheld from his pay; he must pay them himself
He is guaranteed overtime pay after 40 hours
His employer pays half of his Social Security tax
He receives a Form W-2 each January

questions.correct_answer: No taxes are withheld from his pay; he must pay them himself
questions.intro: An independent contractor works for himself or herself, not as an employee. Payers usually do not withhold taxes, overtime laws generally do not apply, and there are usually no employer benefits. Contractors may receive a Form 1099-NEC (or a 1099-K from a payment platform) instead of a W-2.
questions.feedback: Contractors receive no withholding; they make their own tax payments, including self-employment tax.
sources: IRS (Self-Employment Tax, Topic 554): Self-employment tax is 15.3% (12.4% Social Security + 2.9% Medicare) on 92.35% of net earnings; a return is required when net self-employment earnings are $400 or more. (https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/self-employment-tax-social-security-and-medicare-taxes)
IRS (Gig Economy Tax Center): Gig income is taxable whether or not the worker receives a Form 1099. (https://www.irs.gov/businesses/gig-economy-tax-center)

(https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/am-i-required-to-file-a-form-1099-or-other-information-return)

questions.prompt: Ravi earned $900 in delivery fees this month and spent $180 on gas and other business expenses. What were his net earnings?
questions.intro: For self-employed work, net earnings (profit) = income − business expenses. Taxes are figured on net earnings, so tracking expenses matters.

questions.prompt: Self-employment tax is 15.3% of 92.35% of net earnings. Ravi has $720 of net self-employment profit, no wages anywhere else, and owes no Additional Medicare Tax. Estimate his self-employment tax (to the nearest cent).
questions.intro: Self-employment tax is the self-employed person's Social Security and Medicare tax. With no employer to pay half, the rate is 15.3% (12.4% + 2.9%), figured on 92.35% of net profit. It is owed in addition to income tax. (Very high earners and people who also have wages can face other rules.)

choices.text: No; income without a form is tax-free
Only if the client reports it first
Only if the total from that client is over $10,000

questions.intro: Federal income tax applies to income from all sources unless a specific rule excludes it. Forms such as the 1099 report income to the IRS, but they do not decide whether income is taxable.

questions.prompt: A gig worker has no withholding and expects to owe $2,000 in tax for the year. She paid no tax last year because she had no income, so no safe harbor protects her. She pays nothing until April. What risk does this create?

choices.text: No risk; all taxes are due in April
The IRS cancels taxes under $5,000
Her tax refund will be larger than usual
An underpayment penalty, plus one large bill

questions.correct_answer: An underpayment penalty, plus one large bill
questions.intro: Taxes are pay-as-you-go. People who expect to owe $1,000 or more after withholding and credits usually make quarterly estimated payments (Form 1040-ES). "Safe harbor" rules can prevent a penalty, for example by paying enough based on this year's or last year's tax.
questions.feedback: Without withholding, estimated payments, or a safe harbor, she may owe an underpayment penalty.
